title: Managing multiple clients means managing multiple disconnected workflows.
description: As a labour law consultancy grows, client data, compliance work, documents, payroll and follow-ups become harder to manage across disconnected tools.

items.title: Client data is scattered
items.description: Client details, employee records, UAN/ESIC information and other records are spread across Excel sheets, folders and physical files.

items.title: Compliance deadlines are hard to track
items.description: PF, ESI, PT, LWF, returns, licence renewals and other recurring obligations require constant tracking across multiple clients.

items.title: Applicability is difficult to manage
items.description: Different clients have different registrations, employee counts, industries and compliance requirements, making applicability harder to track manually.

items.title: Document management becomes chaotic
items.description: Licences, certificates, returns and client documents are stored across folders, making search, expiry tracking and version history difficult.

items.title: Client follow-ups consume time
items.description: Teams repeatedly chase clients for attendance, documents, approvals and other information through WhatsApp, email and calls.

items.title: Payroll work is repetitive
items.description: Attendance, salary calculations, PF, ESI, PT, deductions and statutory records create recurring manual work across multiple clients.

items.title: Team work lacks visibility
items.description: When several employees handle different clients, assigning work and knowing what is pending, completed or overdue becomes difficult.

items.title: Inspections create last-minute pressure
items.description: When a notice or inspection arrives, finding the right documents, records and compliance history quickly can become a major challenge.
